q: Why did the Mets over-perform on attendance in 2025?
title: Mets attendance above expectations, 2025
cited: The New York Mets averaged 39,316 fans a game in 2025, 21.4% above the 32,383 fans their prior two years of crowds, win rate, and market would predict, up 33.3% from 29,485 the season before, and part of this may be a rebound from 18.6% below prediction (table: team_season_model; query: Q2). This surge saw the Mets draw 94.9% of capacity (table: games_clean; query: Q3). The increased interest coincided with the historic offseason signing of superstar Juan Soto to a 15-year, $765 million contract, the largest in professional sports history ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)). The front office also added key talent including Frankie Montas, Clay Holmes, Griffin Canning, Sean Manaea, Jesse Winker, and A. J. Minter ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)). On the field, the team opened the season with a 45–24 record through June 12, holding the best record in baseball at the time ([2025 New York Mets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Mets_season)).
report: The New York Mets averaged 39,316 fans a game in 2025, 21.4% above the 32,383 fans their prior two years of crowds, win rate, and market would predict, up 33.3% from 29,485 the season before, and part of this may be a rebound from 18.6% below prediction[1]. This surge saw the Mets draw 94.9% of capacity[2]. The increased interest coincided with the historic offseason signing of superstar Juan Soto to a 15-year, $765 million contract, the largest in professional sports history[3]. The front office also added key talent including Frankie Montas, Clay Holmes, Griffin Canning, Sean Manaea, Jesse Winker, and A. J. Minter[3]. On the field, the team opened the season with a 45–24 record through June 12, holding the best record in baseball at the time[3].

q: How did the Cubs do on attendance and viewership last year?
title: Cubs attendance and national TV audience, 2024 to 2025
cited: The Chicago Cubs averaged 37,259 fans a game in 2025, 0.9% above the 36,939 their prior two years of crowds, win rate, and market would predict, up 3.7% from 35,923 the season before (table: team_season_model). The Cubs drew 89.9% of capacity (table: games_clean) and brought their official home total to 3,017,983 fans (table: team_season_model; query: Q4, Q2). On television, the Cubs averaged 1,126,444 viewers across their single-game national broadcasts, ranking third in the league behind the Los Angeles Dodgers at 1,290,545 viewers and the New York Yankees at 1,160,929 viewers (table: team_tv_summary; query: Q3, Q6). This average was well above the league average of 620,657 viewers (table: team_tv_summary; query: Q5). Chicago made 15 national TV appearances across ESPN, Fox, TBS, and FS1, compared to the league average of 8.7 appearances per team, and peaked with a single-game high of 2,041,000 viewers (table: team_tv_summary; query: Q5, Q3).
report:
The Chicago Cubs averaged 37,259 fans a game in 2025, 0.9% above the 36,939 their prior two years of crowds, win rate, and market would predict, up 3.7% from 35,923 the season before[1]. The Cubs drew 89.9% of capacity and brought their official home total to 3,017,983 fans[2][3][4]. On television, the Cubs averaged 1,126,444 viewers across their single-game national broadcasts, ranking third in the league behind the Los Angeles Dodgers at 1,290,545 viewers and the New York Yankees at 1,160,929 viewers[5][6]. This average was well above the league average of 620,657 viewers[7]. Chicago made 15 national TV appearances across ESPN, Fox, TBS, and FS1, compared to the league average of 8.7 appearances per team, and peaked with a single-game high of 2,041,000 viewers[7][5].

title: Cubs monthly attendance, 2025
cited: The Chicago Cubs peaked in June 2025 with an average of 39,531 fans per game, drawing 95.7% of capacity after a strong spring climb (table: games_clean; query: Q2). The Cubs began April averaging 33,881 fans a game and drawing 82.0% of capacity (table: games_clean; query: Q2). May crowds rose by 2,775 fans to average 36,656 fans a game, drawing 88.8% of capacity, which was an increase of 6.7 percentage points (table: games_clean; query: Q3, Q2). The team saw another jump of 2,875 fans in June to reach the season high, up 7.0 percentage points from May (table: games_clean; query: Q3). July attendance dipped by 247 fans to average 39,284 fans a game, drawing 95.1% of capacity, down 0.6 percentage points (table: games_clean; query: Q3, Q2). August crowds fell by another 1,069 fans to average 38,216 fans a game, drawing 92.5% of capacity, a drop of 2.6 percentage points (table: games_clean; query: Q3, Q2). The Cubs finished September with a further decline of 1,950 fans to average 36,266 fans a game, drawing 87.8% of capacity, down 4.7 percentage points from August (table: games_clean; query: Q3, Q2).

sources.query: SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM official_date) as month, AVG(attendance) as avg_attendance, AVG(fill_pct) as avg_fill_pct FROM games_clean WHERE home_team_id = 112 AND season = 2025 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH monthly AS ( SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM official_date) as month, AVG(attendance) as avg_attendance, AVG(fill_pct) as avg_fill_pct FROM games_clean WHERE home_team_id = 112 AND season = 2025 GROUP BY 1 ) SELECT m1.month, m1.avg_attendance, m1.avg_fill_pct, m1.avg_attendance - LAG(m1.avg_attendance) OVER (ORDER BY m1.month) as attendance_change, m1.avg_fill_pct - LAG(m1.avg_fill_pct) OVER (ORDER BY m1.month) as fill_pct_change FROM monthly m1 ORDER BY m1.month

title: AL East attendance actual vs expected, 2025
cited: The Boston Red Sox were the only AL East team to beat their attendance expectations in 2025, averaging 34,278 fans a game (table: team_season_model, teams) to draw 90.8% of capacity (table: games_clean), which was 511 fans above their expected average (table: team_season_model, teams; query: Q4, Q6). The New York Yankees led the division with 42,408 fans per game (table: team_season_model, teams) and drew 91.1% of capacity (table: games_clean), though that fell 827 fans below expectations (table: team_season_model, teams; query: Q4, Q6). The Toronto Blue Jays averaged 35,184 fans (table: team_season_model, teams) and drew 89.9% of capacity (table: games_clean), finishing 1,639 fans below their expected average (table: team_season_model, teams; query: Q4, Q6). The Baltimore Orioles averaged 22,546 fans (table: team_season_model, teams) and drew 49.9% of capacity (table: games_clean), which was 3,174 fans below expectations (table: team_season_model, teams; query: Q4, Q6). The Tampa Bay Rays averaged 9,713 fans (table: team_season_model, teams) and drew 88.1% of capacity (table: games_clean) at a temporary home park (table: games_clean), but their expected attendance is unknown (table: team_season_model, teams; query: Q4, Q6).

q: List the five biggest Cubs home crowds in 2025, with date, opponent and attendance.
title: Cubs top five home crowds, 2025
cited: The Chicago Cubs drew their largest 2025 home crowd on June 19, when 41,078 fans watched them play the Milwaukee Brewers (table: games_clean; query: Q2). The second-largest crowd of the season brought 41,011 fans to Wrigley Field on July 18 against the Boston Red Sox (table: games_clean; query: Q2). Rounding out the top five, the Cubs welcomed 40,703 fans on July 19 for another matchup against the Red Sox (table: games_clean; query: Q2).

q: How did Yankees national TV audiences change from 2025 to 2026?
title: Yankees national TV audience, 2025 vs 2026
cited: The New York Yankees averaged 1,694,167 viewers per national TV broadcast in 2026, a jump of 533,238 viewers from their 1,160,929 viewers average in 2025, though Nielsen changed its method in September 2025, which generally raised sports audiences (table: team_tv_summary; query: Q1, Q2). This viewership growth coincided with more national exposure, as the team's schedule expanded from 19 appearances across 14 single games in 2025 to 22 appearances across 17 single games in 2026 (table: team_tv_summary). The Yankees' 2025 national TV mix included seven games on TBS, five on ESPN, five on Fox, and two on FS1 (table: team_tv_summary). The network mix also differs between the seasons: 7 on TBS, 5 on Fox, 5 on ESPN, and 2 on FS1 in 2025, and 8 on TBS, 5 on Fox, 3 on NBC, 2 on ESPN, 2 on FS1, 1 on Netflix, and 1 on ABC in 2026 (table: game_tv_lookup).
report:
The New York Yankees averaged 1,694,167 viewers per national TV broadcast in 2026, a jump of 533,238 viewers from their 1,160,929 viewers average in 2025, though Nielsen changed its method in September 2025, which generally raised sports audiences[1][2]. This viewership growth coincided with more national exposure, as the team's schedule expanded from 19 appearances across 14 single games in 2025 to 22 appearances across 17 single games in 2026[1]. The Yankees' 2025 national TV mix included seven games on TBS, five on ESPN, five on Fox, and two on FS1[1]. The network mix also differs between the seasons: 7 on TBS, 5 on Fox, 5 on ESPN, and 2 on FS1 in 2025, and 8 on TBS, 5 on Fox, 3 on NBC, 2 on ESPN, 2 on FS1, 1 on Netflix, and 1 on ABC in 2026[3].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons.*

q: Why did Rays attendance drop in 2025?

seasons.exclusion_reason: Rays at Steinbrenner Field, a temporary park
Rays back at Tropicana Field, so the prior year is the temporary park

title: Rays attendance drop causes, 2024 to 2025
cited: The Tampa Bay Rays averaged 9,713 fans a game in 2025 down 41.2% from 16,515 the season before (table: team_season_model). A model prediction for this season is unavailable because the team played in a temporary ballpark (table: team_season_model). This shift coincided with Hurricane Milton heavily damaging Tropicana Field, rendering it unusable for the entire season ([2025 Tampa Bay Rays season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Tampa_Bay_Rays_season)). Instead, the Rays played their 81 home games at George M. Steinbrenner Field, a spring training park in Tampa ([2025 Tampa Bay Rays season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Tampa_Bay_Rays_season)). While total home attendance fell by 550,989 fans (table: team_season_model, team_season_attendance), the Rays drew a higher share of capacity in 2025 at 88.1% compared to 66.0% of capacity in 2024, a gap of 22.1 percentage points (table: games_clean; query: Q6, Q3).
report: The Tampa Bay Rays averaged 9,713 fans a game in 2025 down 41.2% from 16,515 the season before[1]. A model prediction for this season is unavailable because the team played in a temporary ballpark[1]. This shift coincided with Hurricane Milton heavily damaging Tropicana Field, rendering it unusable for the entire season[2]. Instead, the Rays played their 81 home games at George M. Steinbrenner Field, a spring training park in Tampa[2]. While total home attendance fell by 550,989 fans, the Rays drew a higher share of capacity in 2025 at 88.1% compared to 66.0% of capacity in 2024, a gap of 22.1 percentage points[1][3][4][5].
